summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, heart failure, and obesity was admitted for acute on chronic heart failure exacerbation due to medication and dietary noncompliance. He presented with dyspnea, orthopnea, and leg swelling. Treatment included IV furosemide and diuresis, resulting in a weight loss from 126.8 kg to 118.1 kg. His INR was initially supratherapeutic (3.9), then became subtherapeutic (1.7), requiring bridging with Lovenox and warfarin dose adjustment. Brief episodes of ventricular tachycardia led to resumption and uptitling of metoprolol to 37.5 mg. Ramipril was increased to twice daily, and colchicine was discontinued. He stabilized, was discharged home on oral diuretics, anticoagulation, and beta-blocker therapy, with instructions to continue Lovenox until INR therapeutic and to monitor weight and symptoms.
problems: Acute on chronic combined systolic (congestive) and diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with unspecified diabetic retinopathy without macular edema
Patient's other noncompliance with medication regimen
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
